This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Cha-cha**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read the band's last four bars on the staff underneath. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Bass lines](index.qmd#bass)

## The pattern

Root held through beats 1 and 2, the fifth on 3 and the root again on 4.

It belongs in *Cha-cha*. Here it is in the cha-cha style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Cha-cha","opts":{"bassFeel":"chacha"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: Roots on 1 and 3

Start with something simpler. The root on beats 1 and 3, held; one note a bar in 3/4. A chord that changes in between gets its root when it arrives.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass-halves.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Root and fifth

The boom of boom-chick: the root on beat 1 and the fifth on beat 3, short, the same every bar. In 3/4 it is one note a bar, root one bar and fifth the next.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass-alt.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Root and fifth","opts":{"bassFeel":"alt"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Cha-cha, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Root held through 1 and 2, fifth on 3, root on 4: three notes that sit under the cha-cha-cha of the chords. Keep beat 3 and beat 4 short and even, like the dancers' feet.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Cha-cha","opts":{"bassFeel":"chacha"}},{"label":"Root and fifth (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"alt"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 112 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Cha-cha","opts":{"bassFeel":"chacha"}}]'></div>

## Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am Dm|E7 Am|Dm E7|Am" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Cha-cha","opts":{"bassFeel":"chacha"}}]'></div>
